findings.cross_file_justification: The invariant 'oracle_open: true implies eval_only: true' is enforced only in validate-suite.sh (new arm checks, VS-17). pipeline-run.sh does not call the validator; it accepts any --suite-file and reads only the declarative eval_only flag from ARM_DEF.
findings.description: The refusal gate keys off the declarative `eval_only` flag rather than the property that actually matters: `toggles.oracle_open == true`, which skips the answer-path overlay and exposes the oracle to the model under evaluation. A suite file passed via `--suite-file` (or an edited in-tree suite) with `toggles: {oracle_open: true}` and no `eval_only` key passes this check with EVAL_ONLY=false and runs the open mount outside any batch context, and the resulting rows carry no eval_only marker for ablation-report.py to exclude from components. The only thing preventing that is a separate validator that nothing in this run path invokes.
findings.failure_mode: Open-mount (answer-leaking) trials run outside the batch context and are reported as a shipped-default component, silently contaminating the ablation decision; the guard this change introduces is bypassed without touching LOA_ABLATION_BATCH_CONTEXT.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the gate from the dangerous property as well as the flag: `EVAL_ONLY=true` when `.eval_only == true` OR `.toggles.oracle_open == true`, and either refuse (exit 2) or treat the arm as eval_only when oracle_open is set without eval_only. Optionally have run-ablation.sh invoke validate-suite.sh on the suite file before launching trials.

findings.description: The eval_only guard is a single, documented, unauthenticated environment variable (`LOA_ABLATION_BATCH_CONTEXT=1`). The header comments and the dry-run docs tell the operator to set it by hand, so the control is advisory: any invocation can satisfy it by prefixing the command, and an operator who `export`s it once in their shell (rather than inline as documented) disables the guard for every subsequent manual pipeline-run.sh call in that session. This is consistent with the stated design but should not be mistaken for an enforcement boundary.
findings.failure_mode: Eval-only / open-mount arms get run and recorded as ordinary trials by accident (lingering exported variable) or by an operator working around the message, with nothing in the run record distinguishing a guarded batch launch from a manual bypass.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the context in the run record (e.g. meta/arm-evidence `batch_context=1` plus the launching run-ablation.sh batch id) so ablation-report.py can exclude eval_only rows that lack a batch provenance, and prefer a per-batch token (batch id or nonce passed by run-ablation.sh and written to the run dir) over a constant `1`.
